questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code protects account balances when money leaves an account? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A client calls Balance("A") while Transfer("A", "B", 50) is executing. Which outcomes can the Balance call observe?
choices: A balance with the debit applied but no credit recorded in the journal yet
Either the balance before the transfer or after it, never a state where B has been credited but A not yet debited
Any intermediate value, because Balance uses only a read lock
The call fails with ErrInsufficientFunds if the transfer is in flight

questions.prompt: Statement copies matching entries into a new slice instead of returning s.journal or a sub-slice of it. Why does that matter?
choices: It sorts the entries by account so callers get a stable order
It lets the caller mutate entries without affecting other accounts' statements
It is required because RWMutex forbids returning slices
The returned data no longer aliases storage that record() appends to under the write lock, so the caller can read it after the lock is released

questions.prompt: What is the main throughput trade-off of the Store's locking design?
choices: A single store-wide mutex serializes all writes across every account, even for unrelated accounts
Readers block each other because Balance takes the same lock as Deposit
Deadlock is likely when two transfers go in opposite directions between the same accounts
Each account has its own lock, so memory use grows with account count
